name: JOSS
description: A language started in 1962 by RAND corporation. JOSS is an acronym for JOHNNIAC Open Shop System.

commands.description: A demand statement prompts values for a list of variables from the end user.  For example, Demand x,y.

args.name: pageNumber
args.description: Might be expressed in the form page # or part #.  For example, page 1

commands.description: Executes a specified part of the program.  A 'part' in JOSS is similar to a label in several other programming languages like assembly and BASIC.  A part is also a bit like a procedure or subroutine in other languages.
Returns from a part or subroutine.
Jumps to a specified line.  This is similar but not the same as 'do'. 'do' executes a part like a subroutine and will return.  'to' is specific down to the line number and won't return.
Returns 1 if the input value is true.  Returns 0 otherwise.

operators.description: A middle dot character represents multiplication in JOSS.  Most newer programming languages including Logo use * instead.

keywords.description: Sets 1 or more variables to specified value or values.  For example, Set a=0, p=1.

symbols.description: The pipe character is used like parenthesis around expressions for calculating absolute values.  For example, |-4| = 4.  |4| also evaluates to 4.  |x| would roughly translate to abs :x in WebLogo.
